page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by AMD EPYC 7571 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth ranking in the top 25%, while large-block read and write bandwidths maintain average levels. Cryptographic performance is also strong, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the top 25%, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instruction sets.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5ad.24xlarge offers a high-density memory configuration paired with local NVMe SSD storage, reducing the need for external network-attached storage for high-throughput data operations. The trade-off lies in its lower single-core compute performance, making it less suitable for single-threaded applications or latency-sensitive sequential processing. Instead, the instance is optimized for memory-intensive, parallelized workloads. Appropriate use cases include large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, big data analytics, and multi-threaded enterprise applications that benefit from high memory capacity and fast local scratch space.
